page: Microsoft Azure D16ds_v7 is a general-purpose server instance powered by the Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor runs at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and is equipped with a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1D cache. It includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated matrix operations.

The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. For local storage, it includes a 945 GB local disk and supports Premium Storage. The memory subsystem delivers a read-only bandwidth of 1217.74 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 129.38 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write bandwidth of 54.82 GB/sec.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the average tier for most general compute tasks, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2204.79 and a multi-core score of 16997.2. However, it demonstrates top-tier capabilities in specific workloads, achieving 35.66 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 354.35 tokens/sec in text generation for small 135M parameter language models. Database operations via Passmark score at 8347.97, and Redis SET operations reach 27.91 million operations per second.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and integrated 945 GB local storage, the D16ds_v7 offers a resource-dense profile suitable for relational databases, web serving, and intermediate data processing. The inclusion of AMX and AVX-512 instructions provides qualitative efficiency for lightweight machine learning inference and compression tasks without requiring dedicated GPU hardware, though the lack of a GPU limits its utility for large-scale deep learning training.
